newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's top bank reports record profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's top bank reports record profit in 1996.

text.p: National Bank of Kuwait (NBK), the country's largest commercial bank, on Thursday reported a nine percent rise in net profit in 1996 to 71.3 million dinars ($238 million).
Chairman Mohammed al-Bahar said in a statement return on equity was 20 percent in 1996 compared with 19 the previous year while return on capital was 51 percent for the year.
Bahar gave no further details of the bank's balance sheet.

He said achievements in 1996 included the finalisation of a $1.2 billion loan for Equate Petrochemicals Company, a joint venture with Union Carbide Corp, in the "largest limited recourse project financing ever arranged in the Gulf" in which 54 international and regional banks participated.

Moody's Investors Service assigned NBK the highest rating given to any bank in the Middle East, Bahar adeded. In April it was assigned a rating of Baa1 for long-term deposits, Prime-2 for short-term deposits and C+ for bank financial strength.
NBK shares closed on Wednesday at 650 fils, 30 fils lower than the high recorded last month.
The bank, founded in 1952 and wholly owned by Kuwaiti interests, is the oldest commercial bank on the Arabian Peninsula.
